                    ### Question
                    A 70-year-old Caucasian male visits your office regularly for treatment of New York Heart association class IV congestive heart failure. Which of the following medications would you add to this man's drug regimen in order to improve his overall survival?

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
In a 70-year-old Caucasian male with New York Heart association class IV congestive heart failure, adding Spironolactone to the drug regimen is recommended to improve overall survival. Spironolactone, an aldosterone antagonist, reduces fluid retention and edema, improves symptoms in heart failure, and increases survival in heart failure patients. Amiloride, a potassium-sparing diuretic, may have limited impact on overall survival in heart failure. Hydrochlorothiazide, a thiazide diuretic, has a limited role in heart failure treatment and unclear impact on overall survival. Furosemide, a loop diuretic, improves symptoms but does not impact survival. Acetazolamide, a carbonic anhydrase inhibitor, is not typically used in heart failure management and has no evidence of survival benefit.
